streets.title: Herbarium of streets
streets.sub: The real outlines of streets, squares and parks bearing Lenin's name — taken from OpenStreetMap and laid out like herbarium sheets.
streets.foot: The longest sheet is “{name}”, {city}, {max}. The shortest is {min}, {minCity}. Sheets are sorted by length.
streets.empty: No streets match. Clear the country filter or change the search.
catalog.title: Card index
catalog.sub: The whole corpus without a map: Lenin's name was carried by things of very different orders — from an address to an asteroid. Here they are sorted by what they were.
catalog.total: {records} records, {countries} countries. The stripe on the left of a card marks the fate of the name: brass — still borne, red — renamed, grey — lost.
catalog.empty: Nothing in this rubric matches. The numbers in the rail on the left show where the matches are.
rubric.oneOff.note: Celestial bodies, ships, canals, peaks, a geoglyph in the taiga and a park-museum in a Lithuanian forest — things that exist in a single copy.
rubric.address.note: Avenues, boulevards, lanes. For such an object the name is the object: take down the sign and nothing is left. The bulk of the non-Soviet corpus.
rubric.settlement.note: Settlements, districts and whole regions named after Lenin. Almost all in the former Soviet Union, and almost all renamed.
rubric.work.note: Works, power stations, mines, collective farms, metro lines and railways. Here the name is not an address but a title: the object still works under another one.
rubric.mind.note: Universities, schools, libraries, museums, theatres, stadiums and hospitals — institutions given the name as an obligation.
rubric.rest.note: Everything that did not fit the rubrics: houses of culture, newspapers, trusts, organisations — and records still awaiting sorting.
stats.title: In the name of Lenin
stats.lede: Objects that bore or still bear the name of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin — from a street in a Brazilian village to a canal fifteen hundred kilometres long.
stats.source: Compiled from the museum's materials: “Lenin streets outside the USSR” and “USSR”.
stats.sub.where: Six parts of the world. Two thirds of the corpus is the former Soviet Union, but the name travelled far beyond it.
stats.foot.where: Outside the former USSR — {n} objects, almost half the corpus. The name spread wider than the country that planted it.
stats.sub.countries: The twenty countries with the densest trace. The rest are a long tail of one or two records.
stats.foot.countries: Another {tail} countries — {sum} records: Somalia, Benin, Madagascar, Yemen, Malaysia, Costa Rica — one or two each.
stats.screen.kinds: The name on the map and the name at work
stats.sub.kinds: Abroad, Lenin's name went to streets and squares. In the Soviet Union — to plants, stations, institutes, whole cities.
stats.foot.kinds: Abroad Lenin's name is an address: streets, squares and boulevards give {share}% of the foreign records. In the USSR it is work: plants, power stations, institutes, whole cities.
stats.kinds.note: bar length is the share within its own corpus
stats.sub.wave: The years the name arrived and the years it left. Two waves seventy years apart.
stats.foot.wave: {n} records of {total} are counted — those with a year named in the sources. The peak of naming is the 1920s, the second rise the 1950s and 60s. The ebb begins in the late 1980s and collapses onto 1991.
stats.screen.fate: Where it stayed, where it went
stats.sub.fate: The name vanished first where it had been planted — and stayed where it had been chosen.
stats.foot.fate: In France {fr} objects still bear Lenin's name today, in Kazakhstan — {kz}. Status is inferred from the wording of the museum's materials and needs spot-checking.
stats.sub.mass: Lenin streets, lanes and squares in Russia alone. Every dot is one of them.
stats.foot.mass: {streets} streets and {lanes} lanes — {total} in total as of {year}. The whole rest of the corpus, all seventy-four countries, is {rest} records: fewer than the Lenin streets of the Ulyanovsk region alone.
